note: Enterprise AI tracker. One object in items is one dated deal, neocloud update, or data-center update. Add a company first if it is new. company_ids must match companies[].id. sections is deal, neocloud, and/or datacenter, and an item shows in each section listed. status is done, in_the_works, or rumored. deal_type is partnership, contract, reseller, infrastructure, datacenter, sovereign, customer_win, pricing, product_launch, ipo, earnings, capacity, financing, or power. unconfirmed true means the date or figure is reported and was not read from a company filing or company page. related_ids are other ids in this file. Leave key_number empty when the source states no figure. Do not invent a price, a percent move, or a dollar amount. After editing, run npm run briefs.

items.title: Dell books a record AI-server quarter and a $95 billion backlog
items.summary: Dell said Q2 FY27 AI-server orders were a record $60.9 billion, AI-optimized server revenue was a record $16.4 billion, and the AI-server backlog ended at a record $95 billion. It also raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook by $25 billion to $192 billion. Reuters reported that the AI-optimized server outlook for the year was raised to $74 billion from $60 billion.
items.why_it_matters: The backlog is the stock number for Dell's AI-server cycle and a demand read-through for Nvidia.
items.source_label: Dell Q2 FY27 release, Sep 1, 2026. The $74 billion year outlook is Reuters's report of the same results.

items.title: Dell and Palantir publish a sovereign AI stack for supply chains
items.summary: Dell said Palantir Foundry and Ontology can run on the Dell AI Factory with Nvidia so customers keep data on infrastructure they control. No dollar value was stated.
items.why_it_matters: It is a sovereign, on-prem path for Dell servers rather than a cloud-only AI sale.

items.title: Dell expands the AI Data Platform for enterprise agents
items.summary: Dell said the AI Data Platform processes data nearly four times faster on average than CPUs alone. The unified semantic layer, enterprise knowledge graph, and knowledge agents are scheduled for the first half of 2027.
items.key_number: Nearly 4x faster than CPUs alone, Dell said
items.why_it_matters: Storage and data software are how Dell sells the AI server cycle into ordinary enterprises, but part of the stack is not shipping yet.

items.title: Dell says more than 6,500 enterprises use its AI Factory
items.summary: At Nvidia GTC in Berlin, Dell said more than 6,500 enterprises have adopted the Dell AI Factory with Nvidia, up from 5,000 the prior quarter. New deskside and data-center products were announced, with some availability dates running into 2027.
items.why_it_matters: Customer count is the enterprise adoption number behind Dell's AI-server backlog.

items.title: Dell reports Q3 FY27 results
items.summary: Dell scheduled the fiscal 2027 third-quarter call for Tuesday, Nov 24, 2026, at 3:30 p.m. CST. Results come out before the call.
items.why_it_matters: The next print is the update to AI-server orders, revenue, and backlog.

items.title: Cisco adds Supermicro racks to the Secure AI Factory
items.summary: Cisco said it will sell Supermicro liquid- and air-cooled systems as part of the Secure AI Factory with Nvidia, including Vera Rubin NVL72 and HGX Rubin NVL8. Cisco said the offering would begin in October 2026. No dollar value was stated.
items.why_it_matters: Cisco is reselling rack-scale GPU systems, which ties its AI networking story to Supermicro and Nvidia.

items.title: AMD, Cisco, and HUMAIN put AI compute into production in Saudi Arabia
items.summary: The companies said AMD Instinct MI355X systems on Cisco Silicon One networking are live for HUMAIN customers. They plan up to 250 MW more beginning in 2027 and still aim for up to 1 GW by 2030.
items.why_it_matters: It is a named sovereign build with a power figure, not only a networking product launch.

items.title: Cisco raises hyperscaler AI revenue expectations to $9 billion
items.summary: Cisco reported Q1 FY27 revenue of $18.5 billion and raised its expectation for AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers to $9 billion in FY27, more than double FY26. On the call, Cisco said enterprise product orders rose 15% and that it won three new AI design wins.
items.key_number: $9 billion hyperscaler AI revenue expected in FY27
items.why_it_matters: The $9 billion target is the figure that tells you whether Cisco's AI networking orders are turning into revenue.
items.source_label: Cisco Q1 FY27 release, Nov 12, 2026. Order details are from the earnings call.

items.title: Thoughtworks joins the Claude Partner Network as a Select partner
items.summary: Thoughtworks said it joined Anthropic's services track as a Select partner, with certified practitioners and a Claude center of excellence. No contract value was stated.
items.why_it_matters: Services partners are how Claude gets into existing enterprise systems ahead of the IPO.

items.title: Bain becomes a Global Premier Claude partner
items.summary: Bain said it is a Global Premier partner and has rolled Claude out to its 19,000 employees. More than 7,000 people used it in the pilot.
items.why_it_matters: A named global rollout is a seat-count signal for Claude in large companies.

items.title: Oliver Wyman joins the Claude Partner Network
items.summary: Oliver Wyman, part of Marsh, said it joined as a Select Services partner. It said it has advised on more than $50 billion of AI-related capital deployment. That figure is Oliver Wyman's own advisory work, not an Anthropic contract.
items.why_it_matters: Another large consultancy will sell Claude into enterprise transformations.

items.title: Anthropic brings Salesforce into Claude
items.summary: Anthropic said a Salesforce in Claude plugin lets sellers research accounts, prepare calls, review pipeline, and draft CRM updates. No fee or seat count was stated.
items.why_it_matters: Claude sitting on top of Salesforce is a distribution path into existing enterprise budgets.

items.title: Akamai signs an $11.6 billion, seven-year deal with Anthropic
items.summary: Akamai's 8-K says Anthropic committed to pay about $11.6 billion under two project plans for dedicated cloud capacity and managed support, each with a seven-year initial term from its service start. Akamai's release also describes a warrant that can vest on about $9 billion of further commitment.
items.why_it_matters: A contracted cash commitment of this size is backlog for Akamai and a compute cost for Anthropic as it lists.
items.source_label: Akamai 8-K filed Sep 24, 2026, agreement dated Sep 18, 2026

items.title: HCLTech signs on as a Global Premier Claude partner
items.summary: HCLTech said it will build industry solutions on Claude, Cowork, and Claude Code, and embed them in selected HCLSoftware products. Anthropic's page says Global Premier status requires 1,000 certified practitioners.
items.key_number: 1,000 certified practitioners required for the tier
items.why_it_matters: A large IT-services firm will resell Claude into banks, hospitals, telecom, and factories.

items.title: JPMorganChase expands Claude Code beyond engineers
items.summary: Anthropic said JPMorganChase is rolling Claude out to more employees than its engineers, including in the commercial and investment bank. No seat count or dollar value was stated.
items.why_it_matters: A top bank widening a coding-agent rollout is a reference customer going into the IPO.

items.title: Anthropic is expected to price its IPO
items.summary: The Nov 10 preliminary prospectus offers 825 million Class A shares at an estimated $70 to $78 and applies to list on Nasdaq as ANT. CNBC reported on Nov 16 that pricing is expected the evening of Nov 18 and trading on Nov 19. The prospectus is marked subject to completion and does not print those two dates.
items.why_it_matters: The listing is the liquidity event for the enterprise-AI trade and a comparable for still-private OpenAI.
items.source_label: Preliminary prospectus dated Nov 10, 2026. Pricing and trading dates: CNBC, Nov 16, 2026.

items.title: Anthropic is expected to start trading as ANT
items.summary: CNBC reported that Class A shares are scheduled to begin trading on Nasdaq on Nov 19 under the symbol ANT, after pricing expected on Nov 18. CNBC said the range implies a valuation of $1.405 trillion.
items.why_it_matters: The first trading day is the market test of enterprise demand for Claude.

items.title: IBM Consulting opens an OpenAI practice
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that IBM will jointly market OpenAI tools and train tens of thousands of consultants on Codex, the API, and cybersecurity. Terms were not disclosed.
items.why_it_matters: IBM's consulting bench is a distribution channel into large accounts. The story is a news report, and no contract value was given.

items.title: GSA signs a discounted ChatGPT agreement for governments
items.summary: GSA said a 27-month OneGov offer, expected to start Oct 1, 2026, gives federal, state, local, and tribal governments 50% off token usage, no platform-access fee, and no minimum. OpenAI's page says the standard $15-per-user monthly license falls to $0, with 50% off usage, from Oct 1, 2026 through Dec 31, 2028.
items.key_number: $0 seat license and 50% off usage, OpenAI said
items.why_it_matters: A published government price is a ceiling other public-sector buyers will cite, and it pulls Microsoft and Oracle only as the deployment partners around OpenAI.
items.source_label: GSA, Sep 10, 2026, and OpenAI's government page

items.title: IBM previews control of Microsoft and Google agents
items.summary: IBM said watsonx Orchestrate can discover agents built on Microsoft Foundry and Google Gemini Enterprise, and that Agent Identity is in preview. A related preview for Microsoft Foundry and Gemini was dated Sep 15, 2026.
items.why_it_matters: IBM is selling governance across other vendors' agents, which is an enterprise budget that sits beside the model vendors.

items.title: Atlassian puts GPT-6 models into Rovo and its own engineering
items.summary: OpenAI said frontier models in the GPT-6 family will power agents across Atlassian and Rovo. More than 3,000 Atlassian developers use Codex.
items.key_number: More than 3,000 Atlassian developers on Codex
items.why_it_matters: A work-management suite shipping OpenAI models is enterprise distribution that does not depend on a single cloud.

items.title: OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud
items.summary: OpenAI said its frontier models and Codex will enter Google Cloud Model Garden, with purchases through Google Cloud Marketplace that can draw down existing commitments. General availability was planned in the coming weeks. Microsoft remains the primary cloud partner.
items.why_it_matters: Google Cloud becomes another reseller of OpenAI, which matters for both companies' enterprise AI revenue.

items.title: HPE and Nvidia extend the private AI factory
items.summary: HPE said Private Cloud AI will add secure agent access and more GPU choice, and that it will support Nvidia's OpenShell reference architecture on Vera Rubin, Vera CPUs, and BlueField-4. No dollar value was stated.
items.why_it_matters: HPE is the other large enterprise server vendor beside Dell selling a controlled, on-prem AI stack.

items.title: Salesforce runs more of its stack on Google Cloud
items.summary: At Dreamforce, Salesforce said the partnership puts Salesforce workloads on Google Cloud through Hyperforce and lets agents on either side use the same data. Several pieces were generally available, and an Agentforce sales agent was in beta on Google Cloud Marketplace.
items.why_it_matters: It moves Salesforce consumption onto Google infrastructure and gives both a joint enterprise agent pitch.

items.title: OpenAI brings Oracle apps into ChatGPT
items.summary: OpenAI said it is expanding the Oracle partnership so Oracle applications and data come into ChatGPT, and so new Oracle products use OpenAI models. No new contract value was stated on OpenAI's page.
items.why_it_matters: Oracle's application installed base is another enterprise door for OpenAI, separate from the cloud-capacity contracts.

items.title: Oracle makes Vera Rubin generally available and plans multi-gigawatt clusters
items.summary: Oracle and Nvidia said Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPUs are generally available on OCI, and that OCI Superclusters with Vera Rubin NVL72 are planned to expand to multi-gigawatt scale. No specific gigawatt total or dollar value was stated.
items.why_it_matters: OCI is competing as an AI cloud, and the capacity plan is a demand line for Nvidia.

items.title: Snowflake will run as a native service on Oracle Cloud
items.summary: Oracle and Snowflake said the Snowflake AI Data Cloud will be a native, first-party service on OCI that customers can buy with Oracle Universal Credits. No revenue figure was stated.
items.why_it_matters: Data-cloud spend on OCI is enterprise AI consumption that can draw down Oracle credits.

items.title: ServiceNow expands its OpenAI partnership
items.summary: OpenAI said ServiceNow will put OpenAI models and agents into workflows from development to security, and will expand ChatGPT Work and Codex to employees. A ServiceNow integration inside ChatGPT was also announced. No dollar value was stated.
items.why_it_matters: ServiceNow is a system of record for IT work, so the partnership is an enterprise workflow sale for both stocks.

items.title: Salesforce and Snowflake extend zero-copy context for agents
items.summary: Salesforce said Data 360 and Snowflake's zero-copy partnership give agents shared enterprise context without moving the data off either platform. No new contract value was stated.
items.why_it_matters: The data layer, not a new model, is what both companies are selling as the enterprise AI product.

items.title: ADNOC signs a multi-year OpenAI and G42 partnership
items.summary: ADNOC said it is the first energy company to deploy OpenAI Frontier, with G42, to connect decisions from wells through trading. The first uses are field master planning and commercial decisions. No dollar value or capacity figure was stated.
items.why_it_matters: A national oil company deploying frontier agents is a sovereign industrial customer, not a chatbot seat deal.

items.title: ChatGPT Enterprise is listed on AWS Marketplace
items.summary: OpenAI said organizations can buy ChatGPT Enterprise through AWS Marketplace and apply eligible spend toward AWS commitments. Healthcare and financial-services editions are included for eligible customers. No price was stated.
items.why_it_matters: AWS commitments can now be spent on ChatGPT Enterprise, which is distribution for OpenAI and consumption for Amazon.

items.title: Applied Digital says 1.4 GW is leased, including more for one hyperscaler
items.summary: Applied Digital said it had 1.4 GW of contracted critical IT load and about $36 billion of contracted lease revenue. Polaris Forge 1 had 175 MW live. A later 15-year lease with the same unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler covers 210 MW at Delta Forge 2 and about $5.2 billion of base-term revenue, with operations expected in the first half of 2028. It also closed $1.59 billion of 7% notes due 2031.
items.why_it_matters: The lease book is Applied Digital's stock story, and CoreWeave is one of the named tenants.

items.title: Galaxy delivers Helios Phase I to CoreWeave
items.summary: Galaxy said data centers earned $79 million of adjusted gross profit in Q3, the first full quarter of Helios I Phase I, and that all 133 MW of that phase had been delivered to CoreWeave by the end of Q2. Phase II is financed, with data-hall deliveries scheduled to begin in the second quarter of 2027. Another 830 MW at Helios II is approved and not yet leased.
items.key_number: 133 MW delivered; $79 million adjusted gross profit
items.why_it_matters: Helios is a CoreWeave supply contract, so the same megawatts sit on both stocks.

items.title: Meta narrows 2026 capex to $135 billion–$145 billion
items.summary: Meta said third-quarter capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, were $34.91 billion. It put full-year 2026 capex on that same basis at $135 billion to $145 billion, narrowed from $130 billion to $145 billion. Free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion.
items.why_it_matters: The capex range is the corporate budget behind Hyperion and Prometheus, and the negative free cash flow is the financing pressure.

items.title: Meta sizes Hyperion at 5 GW and more than $50 billion
items.summary: CNBC reported that Meta said the Richland Parish, Louisiana, campus will be a 5 GW data center costing more than $50 billion, above the roughly $27 billion Blue Owl joint venture disclosed for the earlier plan. CNBC said a spokesperson later put 2 GW by 2030 and the full 5 GW around 2032.
items.why_it_matters: Hyperion is large enough to move Meta's capex and the power and construction suppliers around it. The Blue Owl vehicle covers the earlier budget, not this full figure.
items.source_label: CNBC, Jul 13, 2026, quoting Meta. Blue Owl terms: Meta release, Oct 21, 2025.

items.title: Meta's New Albany sheet puts Prometheus over 1 GW
items.summary: Meta's New Albany campus sheet, posted in September 2026, says the company has invested more than $1.5 billion there since breaking ground in 2017 and that the site will deliver over 1 GW for the Prometheus AI cluster.
items.why_it_matters: Prometheus is the gigawatt cluster Meta is already counting, as distinct from Hyperion, which is still being built.
items.source_label: Meta New Albany campus sheet, September 2026

items.title: Prometheus first phase is reported complete
items.summary: A secondary account of a Meta engineering post said the first phase of the gigawatt-scale cluster was complete on Oct 19, 2026, had been used to train Muse models, holds hundreds of thousands of GPUs, and is planned at about 1 million GPUs. This seed did not read the engineering post, so the update is marked reported.
items.why_it_matters: If the phase is live, Prometheus is already training on Nvidia systems while Hyperion is still a construction project.
items.source_label: The Model Press, citing a Meta engineering account, Oct 19, 2026

items.title: Alphabet keeps 2026 capex at $195 billion–$205 billion
items.summary: On the Q3 call, Alphabet said capex was $51.4 billion, mostly technical infrastructure, of which about 65% was servers and networking and about 35% was data centers. Full-year 2026 capex stays at $195 billion to $205 billion, and 2027 is expected to rise significantly. The company also said it began using third-party compute at the end of the quarter.
items.why_it_matters: The capex range is Google's own buildout, and the third-party compute line is demand for neoclouds.

items.title: Amazon holds 2026 capex at about $220 billion
items.summary: CNBC reported that Amazon still expects 2026 capital spending of about $220 billion and that capital expenditures reached $77.3 billion in the third quarter.
items.key_number: About $220 billion in 2026; $77.3 billion in the quarter
items.why_it_matters: AWS capex is the budget for Amazon's own AI capacity and for the marketplace that now lists ChatGPT Enterprise.
items.source_label: CNBC report of Amazon's Q3 2026 results, Oct 29, 2026

items.title: Microsoft's 2026 capex is reported at $170 billion
items.summary: In its Amazon earnings story, CNBC said Microsoft had earlier that week lowered its 2026 capex forecast to $170 billion from $175 billion. This seed did not read Microsoft's release, so the figure is marked reported.
items.why_it_matters: Microsoft's capex is the budget that pays neocloud contracts such as IREN and Nebius.
items.source_label: CNBC, Oct 29, 2026, mentioning Microsoft. Not read from a Microsoft release.

items.title: IREN's AI cloud revenue triples to $200 million
items.summary: IREN said September-quarter AI Cloud revenue rose to $200 million and total revenue was $228 million. Revenue backlog rose to $20.3 billion. Horizon 1 is in service for Microsoft with Nvidia Exemplar status. A more-than-$4 billion ARR target, fully contracted, moved from year-end 2026 to January 2027 and may slip to February. After quarter-end it signed a five-year deal at about $22 million per megawatt, with 90% of the GPU capex prepaid, and a short-term deal at $40 million per megawatt. Secured power is more than 5 GW.
items.key_number: $20.3 billion backlog; $200 million AI Cloud revenue
items.why_it_matters: Microsoft is the named customer, so a delivery slip at Horizon is a capacity slip for Microsoft and a revenue-timing issue for IREN.

items.title: TeraWulf leases about 401 MW to Anthropic
items.summary: TeraWulf reported Q3 revenue of $76.2 million, including $63.0 million of HPC lease revenue. Lake Mariner had 102 MW of critical IT online and 336 MW under construction, inside a cost guide of $8 million to $10 million per critical IT megawatt. A 20-year Anthropic lease covers about 401 MW and about $19 billion of contracted revenue, with first capacity expected in late 2027. On Nov 4 the company announced a Google credit backstop for project financing and a Fluor EPC contract. Management said on the call that the operating Lake Mariner building is the Fluidstack contract. The size of the Google backstop was not stated in the release summary used here.
items.key_number: About $19 billion and 401 MW for Anthropic
items.why_it_matters: The same lease is an Anthropic compute commitment and TeraWulf's contracted revenue. Fluidstack is the operating tenant at Lake Mariner.
items.source_label: TeraWulf Q3 release, Nov 6, 2026. Fluidstack is named on the earnings call.

items.title: Google is reported to have taken over Crusoe's Wyoming campus
items.summary: Investing.com, citing Reuters, reported on Nov 6, 2026 that Google acquired Crusoe's southeast Wyoming site after announcing a $17 billion investment, and that the acquisition price was not disclosed. A project write-up citing county records says Crusoe withdrew, the campus is now Project Tembo, Google develops it through Jupiter Star Holdings, and the announced load is 1.8 GW. Those ownership and size details were not read from the county filing in this seed.
items.why_it_matters: If Google is buying the campus instead of renting it, Crusoe loses a development, and Alphabet puts the capex on its own books.
items.source_label: Investing.com citing Reuters, Nov 6, 2026. Campus details: a secondary project write-up.

items.title: CoreWeave lifts 2026 revenue guidance and counts a $132.5 billion backlog
items.summary: CoreWeave reported Q3 revenue of $3.661 billion, operating income of $207 million, and a net loss of $709 million after $846 million of net interest expense. Revenue backlog was about $132.5 billion. Active power passed 1.7 GW and contracted power passed 4.6 GW, with more than 1.85 GW of active power still expected at year-end. Full-year revenue guidance rose to $13.0 billion–$13.3 billion and capex to $37 billion–$39 billion. It expects about $9 billion of customer prepayments and deposits in the next three months and closed a $2.6 billion DDTL 5.5 facility. Named expanded customers include OpenAI.
items.why_it_matters: The backlog and the interest bill are the two stock numbers, and OpenAI is a named customer rather than a new disclosed contract value.

items.title: Nebius posts $980.8 million of quarterly revenue and slips part of Microsoft's New Jersey capacity
items.summary: Nebius said Q3 group revenue was $980.8 million, including about $325 million of non-recurring asset-light revenue, and AI-cloud revenue was $973.8 million. ARR was $6.4 billion and remaining performance obligations were $38.7 billion. Contracted power is more than 4 GW, with 5 GW still expected by year-end 2026. It expects 2026 revenue at the low end of $3.0 billion–$3.4 billion, 2027 revenue of $12 billion–$13 billion, and 2027 capex of $40 billion–$45 billion.
